item.content:encoded:
A Halloween-themed fishing tournament is coming to Weeks Bay Resource Center in Fairhope, Alabama on Saturday, October 24th, according to WKRG News 5.

The event, called Trick-or-Trout, combines the spirit of the holiday season with a classic fishing competition. But for many in the community, the tournament carries deeper meaning — it honors the memory of Steve Dorsey, who died during his senior year of high school.

Details about registration, entry fees, and specific tournament rules were not immediately available. Community members interested in participating or supporting the event can contact Weeks Bay Resource Center for more information.

item.title: Visit Pensacola Taps Tony Lyle as New President and CEO
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Visit Pensacola has announced the appointment of Tony Lyle as its next President and CEO, effective October 26. Lyle arrives with more than 25 years of destination marketing and tourism leadership experience, most recently serving as Executive Director of Visit Galveston in Texas for the past three years. Throughout his career, Lyle has overseen…
item.content:encoded:
Visit Pensacola has announced the appointment of Tony Lyle as its next President and CEO, effective October 26. Lyle arrives with more than 25 years of destination marketing and tourism leadership experience, most recently serving as Executive Director of Visit Galveston in Texas for the past three years.

Throughout his career, Lyle has overseen multimillion-dollar public tourism budgets and led strategic initiatives at destination marketing organizations across coastal and Gulf Coast regions. His background spans leisure and group travel, sports tourism, international travel partnerships, brand development, and digital transformation. He holds a Bachelor of Education in Outdoor and Science Education from Liverpool John Moores University in the United Kingdom.

"We are thrilled to have selected Tony Lyle as our new president and CEO," said Visit Pensacola Board Chairman Sterling Gilliam. "His experience leading exceptional organizations makes him a great fit for the Visit Pensacola team, which is already performing at an impressive level."

Lyle said he's eager to collaborate with tourism partners and community leaders. "The most successful destinations are built through collaboration, trust and a shared vision for the future," he said. "I'm looking forward to listening and learning from our tourism partners, community leaders and residents, and working together to build on Pensacola's momentum while creating new opportunities for visitation and meaningful economic impact for Escambia County."

Lyle will introduce himself to the community at Visit Pensacola's Annual Meeting on Wednesday, October 28, at 11:30 a.m., and at the board meeting on Wednesday, November 18, at 3 p.m. at the Bowden Building. Those interested in scheduling a meeting with Lyle can contact Visit Pensacola Executive Assistant Sarah Samsa at ssamsa@visitpensacola.com.

Residents interested in learning more about Forged By Fire's schedule or how to access meals in their area are encouraged to reach out to local community organizations or monitor the nonprofit's communications for updates.

The dual initiatives would reshape planning and land use in Pensacola. The comprehensive plan — the city's long-range…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola City Council is considering significant amendments to the city's comprehensive plan alongside a proposed redevelopment of the Baptist Hospital Legacy Campus, according to a community alert posted on the Citizen Portal.

The dual initiatives would reshape planning and land use in Pensacola. The comprehensive plan — the city's long-range guide for growth and development — has not been substantially updated in years, and amendments could affect zoning, infrastructure priorities, and future development patterns across the city.

The Baptist Hospital Legacy Campus, a prominent property in Pensacola, is being evaluated for redevelopment. Details on the scope of that project, timeline, or specific proposals have not yet been announced.

NewsRadio Pensacola will update you as more information becomes available from the city council.

item.title: AAA: 22.4 Million Americans Expected to Cruise in 2027
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A record 22.4 million Americans are projected to take ocean cruises in 2027, according to AAA's latest forecast released today. That represents a 3.6% increase from 2026 and marks the fifth consecutive year of record cruise passenger volume, driven by growing demand for vacations that bundle costs upfront and offer shared family experiences.…
item.content:encoded:
A record 22.4 million Americans are projected to take ocean cruises in 2027, according to AAA's latest forecast released today. That represents a 3.6% increase from 2026 and marks the fifth consecutive year of record cruise passenger volume, driven by growing demand for vacations that bundle costs upfront and offer shared family experiences.

Cruising has surged since bouncing back from the pandemic, with 2027 projections showing a 57% jump from the 14.2 million Americans who cruised in 2019. The Caribbean accounts for the bulk of that demand—71% of U.S. cruise passengers—with Florida's three major ports (Miami, Port Canaveral, and Fort Lauderdale) ranking among the world's busiest. More than 90% of cruise passengers rate their experience as good or very good, and 93% rebook another cruise.

AAA notes that cruising preferences are shifting. While seven-night itineraries remain most popular, shorter trips of six nights or fewer accounted for 45% of bookings in 2025, up from 39% in 2019, as more travelers seek getaways that don't require a full week away from work or school. Cruise lines are responding with new mega-ships and expanded private island destinations, offering more dining, entertainment, and activity options than ever before.

For those planning a cruise, AAA recommends booking early for best cabin and itinerary selection, arriving a day early if flying to your departure port, and pre-booking popular excursions, specialty dining, and spa treatments to avoid onboard costs.

item.title: Florida AG sues Discord over child safety protections
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier has filed a lawsuit against Discord, the popular messaging and gaming platform used by roughly 90 million people daily, alleging the company fails to adequately protect minors from sexual predators. According to reporting on the case, Uthmeier's office contends that Discord's safety measures are insufficient…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier has filed a lawsuit against Discord, the popular messaging and gaming platform used by roughly 90 million people daily, alleging the company fails to adequately protect minors from sexual predators.

According to reporting on the case, Uthmeier's office contends that Discord's safety measures are insufficient to guard children from exploitation on the platform. The lawsuit represents an escalating effort by state attorneys general nationwide to hold social media and gaming companies accountable for child protection policies.

Discord, which serves as a hub for gaming communities and group messaging, has faced scrutiny from regulators and child safety advocates over how it moderates content and manages user interactions, particularly involving younger users.

item.content:encoded:
Work has finally started on replacing the Freedom Road Bridge in Century, which has sat closed since January 2020—more than six and a half years ago. The bridge, located just east of Jefferson Avenue on Freedom Road, was unexpectedly shut down in early 2020 and has remained off-limits to the public ever since.

The project began Monday, according to reporting from North Escambia. The long closure has affected traffic patterns and access in the area, making the start of construction a significant step for the small community in western Escambia County.

No timeline for completion has been reported, but the bridge replacement is expected to restore a key connection in Century once the work is finished.

item.title: Rep. Salzman, County Officials Host Free Diaper Distribution Wednesday at Ferry Pass Center

The event takes place Wednesday, October 21, from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. at Ferry Pass Community Center, 8800 N 9th Ave in Pensacola. According to a statement from Salzman's…
item.content:encoded:
State Representative Michelle Salzman and Escambia County Commissioner Ashlee Hofberger are partnering to distribute free diapers to families still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The event takes place Wednesday, October 21, from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. at Ferry Pass Community Center, 8800 N 9th Ave in Pensacola.

According to a statement from Salzman's office, the distribution addresses a gap in essential supplies that families have struggled to access since the hurricane. Diapers are a critical need for households with infants and young children, particularly during recovery periods when budgets are stretched thin.

Beyond distributing diapers, state and county constituent services representatives will be on-site to help residents connect with available recovery resources and assistance programs. The event is open to the public, and organizers are providing free treats while supplies last. Attendees arriving before 4:30 p.m. can park on-site. The effort partners with the Florida Department of Children and Families, FANA, Kareem Health, and other local community organizations.

item.title: Court rules Escambia school board must testify in book-ban lawsuit
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A federal appeals court has ordered Escambia County School District board members to give testimony in a lawsuit brought by PEN America, an organization that advocates for free expression and challenges book restrictions in schools. The Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals issued the ruling Monday, requiring the board members to participate in the…
item.content:encoded:
A federal appeals court has ordered Escambia County School District board members to give testimony in a lawsuit brought by PEN America, an organization that advocates for free expression and challenges book restrictions in schools.

The Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals issued the ruling Monday, requiring the board members to participate in the case, which centers on the district's removal of books from school libraries. PEN America, which filed the lawsuit, said the decision represents a significant development in the legal battle over which materials students can access in local schools.

The ruling compels the board to provide information about the decision-making process behind book removals—a requirement the district had previously resisted. The case reflects a broader national debate over school library collections and what role parents, educators, and legal advocates should play in determining which titles remain available to students.

Scott Christmas, 57, crossed the finish line earlier this month after spending the summer and early fall in intensive training for the…
item.content:encoded:
A Fairhope, Alabama resident has completed one of the world's most grueling endurance races—the Ironman World Championship in Hawaii—to honor a promise made three decades ago to a best friend who was killed.

Scott Christmas, 57, crossed the finish line earlier this month after spending the summer and early fall in intensive training for the triathlon. The event, which tests competitors across swimming, cycling, and running disciplines, represents a long-delayed fulfillment of a commitment he made 30 years ago.

According to WKRG News 5, Christmas undertook the challenge as a tribute to his late friend, whose death left a lasting mark on his life. The completion of the Ironman marks both a personal athletic achievement and an act of remembrance for the veteran.

Pensacola is set to become a training hub for international sailing competition, with high-speed racing boats capable of exceeding 60 mph preparing to operate on Pensacola Bay. According to WKRG-TV 5, the Port of Pensacola will serve as the new training facility location for SailGP, positioning the city as a key venue in the global professional sailing circuit.

The addition marks a significant development for Pensacola's waterfront and could bring increased maritime activity and economic activity to the area. SailGP is known for its cutting-edge foiling catamarans—boats that lift above the water at high speeds—making Pensacola Bay an attractive venue for teams preparing for international competition.

Details about the timeline for operations, specific teams involved, and potential impacts on local bay traffic were not immediately available in initial reporting.

Escambia County Area Transit will resume its regular bus schedule Tuesday, October 20, according to a service update from county officials. All routes will operate on normal timetables after what appears to have been a weather-related service disruption over the weekend.

However, riders should plan for possible delays. Debris scattered across several roads throughout the county may slow bus routes, and ECAT is asking the public to allow extra travel time when planning trips.

For real-time information or assistance, passengers can contact ECAT at 850-595-3228. The transit agency thanked riders for their patience during the disruption period.

item.title: Judge Wetherell orders action in PEN America book removal case against Escambia schools
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A federal judge has directed action in the ongoing lawsuit brought by PEN American Center against the Escambia County School Board over book removals from school libraries. According to a court filing, Judge T. Kent Wetherell II has ordered action regarding a status report in the case, which challenges the school district's removal of books under…
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge has directed action in the ongoing lawsuit brought by PEN American Center against the Escambia County School Board over book removals from school libraries.

According to a court filing, Judge T. Kent Wetherell II has ordered action regarding a status report in the case, which challenges the school district's removal of books under Florida's HB 1069. The case, filed in federal court, centers on whether the district's removal practices violate free speech and other constitutional rights.

The specific details of what action the judge is requiring were not immediately clear from the court notice. PEN American Center, a national organization advocating for writers' and readers' rights, has been at the forefront of legal challenges to book removal policies across the country, including in Florida schools.

The Escambia County School Board has faced scrutiny over its book removal process in recent years, with dozens of titles challenged and removed from library shelves. The case is part of a broader national debate over school library materials and curriculum choices.

The filing was submitted October 16 in case CL67400156, which challenges the district's removal of books under Florida's HB 1069 legislation. PEN American Center, a nonprofit…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County School Board has filed a status report in its legal battle with PEN American Center over book removals from school libraries, according to court records. The filing was submitted October 16 in case CL67400156, which challenges the district's removal of books under Florida's HB 1069 legislation.

PEN American Center, a nonprofit organization advocating for free expression, sued the school board over the removals. The case is being heard in Florida state court by Judge T. Kent Wetherell II.

Court records show the district has been ordered to submit additional status reports, with the next deadline set for January 14, 2027. The case remains active as both sides continue to work through the legal process.

item.title: Sen. Scott pushes FCC to keep Chinese drone makers on security blacklist
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott is urging the Federal Communications Commission to maintain Chinese drone manufacturers DJI and Autel on its "Covered List" of communications equipment deemed a national security risk, according to a letter the Florida Republican sent to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr on Monday. Scott, who secured passage of the Countering CCP…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott is urging the Federal Communications Commission to maintain Chinese drone manufacturers DJI and Autel on its "Covered List" of communications equipment deemed a national security risk, according to a letter the Florida Republican sent to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr on Monday.

Scott, who secured passage of the Countering CCP Drones and Supporting Drones for Law Enforcement Act as part of last year's National Defense Authorization Act, argues both companies pose unacceptable security threats through data exfiltration to the Chinese Communist Party and unfair trade practices. "Not only do DJI and Autel present unacceptable national security risks through data exfiltration risks and their support to America's adversaries, but they have also been subsidized by the CCP, enabling them to destroy American manufacturing businesses," Scott wrote.

The senator contends that since 2015, China has flooded global markets with artificially low-priced drones from these manufacturers, driving American competitors out of business and undermining the U.S. drone supply chain. Scott's letter objects to the companies' legal challenges to their placement on the FCC's list, which effectively bans their products from U.S. markets. He has spent years pushing federal agencies to restrict Chinese drone technology from government and military use.

item.title: Early Voting Begins in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Early voting is underway in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties ahead of the Nov. 3 General Election. Voting began Monday morning and continues through Saturday, Oct. 31. Early-voting locations in both counties are open daily from 8 a.m. until 6 p.m. Escambia County has 10 early-voting sites, including the Supervisor of Elections Office in downtown…
item.content:encoded:
Early voting is underway in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties ahead of the Nov. 3 General Election.


Voting began Monday morning and continues through Saturday, Oct. 31.

Early-voting locations in both counties are open daily from 8 a.m. until 6 p.m.


Escambia County has 10 early-voting sites, including the Supervisor of Elections Office in downtown Pensacola, Main Library, Brownsville Community Center, Bellview Library, Southwest Library and the University of West Florida.


Additional Escambia locations are available at Asbury Place, the county Extension Services office in Cantonment, Molino Community Center and the Billy G. Ward Courthouse in Century.

Santa Rosa County has six locations available in Milton, Pace, Gulf Breeze and Navarre.

Unlike Election Day, voters do not have to use their assigned neighborhood precinct during early voting. Registered voters can cast a ballot at any early-voting site within the county where they are registered.


Voters should bring an accepted photo and signature identification.


The deadline to request that a vote-by-mail ballot be mailed to a Florida voter is 5 p.m. Thursday.


Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.

item.title: Plant City Sergeant Honored for Life-Saving CPR Response
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Plant City police sergeant has been recognized by Senator Ashley Moody for his quick thinking and lifesaving actions in September. Sgt. Billy Harvester responded to a call on September 19 for an unresponsive man at a residence. Upon arrival, Harvester found the man in cardiac arrest and immediately retrieved an AED (automated external…
item.content:encoded:
A Plant City police sergeant has been recognized by Senator Ashley Moody for his quick thinking and lifesaving actions in September.

Sgt. Billy Harvester responded to a call on September 19 for an unresponsive man at a residence. Upon arrival, Harvester found the man in cardiac arrest and immediately retrieved an AED (automated external defibrillator) from his patrol car. He applied the device, which delivered a shock to restore the man's heart rhythm, then performed CPR until the patient began breathing on his own.

Moody presented Harvester with a Florida's Finest Award, which recognizes law enforcement officers and citizens for extraordinary lifesaving efforts. "Law enforcement officers have to be ready to face anything when the call comes in—and Sgt. Harvester showed he was ready and capable," Moody said in a statement.

Harvester's decisive action—including his foresight to bring the AED into the residence before assessing the patient—proved critical to the man's survival. The patient's condition improved significantly before paramedics transported him from the scene.
